claims.text: The feedstock is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder.
AlCrFeNiSi produced by LPBF without substrate preheating exhibits significant compositional segregation.
AlCrFeNiSi produced by LPBF without substrate preheating exhibits significant residual stress because of rapid cooling.
AlCrFeNiSi produced by LPBF without substrate preheating exhibits significant defect formation because of rapid cooling.
The proposed intervention is in-situ substrate preheating at 500–600°C during LPBF, together with an optimized scanning strategy.
Substrate preheating raises the base temperature and reduces thermal gradients during solidification.
Substrate preheating at 500–600°C slows the cooling or solidification of LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Lower thermal gradients and slower cooling reduce residual thermal stress.
Slower cooling gives the alloying elements more time to homogenize and thereby limits compositional segregation.
Reduced thermal gradients produce a finer and more uniform AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
The intervention minimizes segregation at grain boundaries.
The intervention lowers defect density in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheated samples will have lower residual stress than otherwise identical LPBF samples made without preheating.
Preheated samples will have less microsegregation than otherwise identical LPBF samples made without preheating.
Preheated samples will have lower defect density than otherwise identical LPBF samples made without preheating.
Preheated samples will exhibit improved mechanical integrity, including enhanced yield strength and ductility.
The hypothesis is restricted to LPBF AlCrFeNiSi processed with substrate temperatures of 500–600°C and an optimized laser scanning strategy.
The effect may not extend to substantially different processing conditions or alloys with substantially different thermal properties.
The magnitude of the mechanical and defect-related improvements depends on energy input, scan strategy, and other machine parameters.

contradictions.description: The top-level hypothesis states comparison with 'conventionally processed parts,' whereas the predicted outcome and baseline define the comparator specifically as LPBF without substrate preheating. Conventional non-additive fabrication and unpreheated LPBF are not necessarily the same baseline.
